name: jdbc-control
description: Plain JDBC positive and negative controls on PostgreSQL JDBC 42.7.14. No Spring, pool, ORM, or transaction framework. correct reads PgConnection.getTransactionState() before Connection.commit() and closes a connection whose rollback failed. unsafe treats a returning commit() as success, commits after a failed savepoint rollback, and calls setAutoCommit(true) after a failed rollback. Category C faults are withheld or rewritten on Connection.rollback and Connection.rollback(Savepoint), once, before pgjdbc sends. The modes are not harness kind control, so this adapter is not a second case-control gate and is not auto-run beside other adapters.

modes.description: Positive control. Connection.setAutoCommit(false), then the work on that connection. Connection.commit() is reported as committed only when PgConnection.getTransactionState() was OPEN before the call. FAILED, which pgjdbc sets from ReadyForQuery status E, is reported as rolled_back after commit() returns; the command tag is not exposed. A thrown commit() is reported as failed and the connection is closed. A failed Connection.rollback(Savepoint) is followed by Connection.rollback(), not commit(). A thrown Connection.rollback() closes the connection and does not call setAutoCommit(true). Connection.setTransactionIsolation is called before setAutoCommit(false). One DriverManager connection is held. It is not a pool.

Negative control. Connection.commit() returning is reported as committed, including when the driver state was FAILED. A thrown commit() is reported as rolled_back. A failed Connection.rollback(Savepoint) is ignored and the outer transaction is committed. A thrown Connection.rollback() is followed by Connection.setAutoCommit(true), and the connection is kept. Connection.setTransactionIsolation is not called. A write made before a savepoint is executed inside that savepoint. One DriverManager connection is held. It is not a pool.

TX-04.independent-inner.reason: JDBC has no propagation mode and no API that commits an inner transaction while an outer transaction stays open. Connection.setSavepoint stays in the same transaction, so an inner transaction cannot commit writes the outer transaction has not committed.
